name: Summer 2026

reviewed.titleJP: 攻殻機動隊 THE GHOST IN THE SHELL
reviewed.review: Watched the first episode of this and man does it look nice they really put so much effort into making this look and feel like Shirow Masamune and his art and style and everything were picked up from 1990 and dropped into today. It doesn't look like one of the early 90s Masamune OVA that were done because the animation style and everything is very different but it also still has that same feel that was done for those work captures and brings it to a modern sense. The content is as compelling as it ever was, which is to say it's peak. There's a good reason why it was adapted and incredibly interesting and vibrant when it was made in the late 80s and then still incredibly interesting environment when it was made in the 90s and then still incredibly vibrant and interesting when it was made in the early 2000s and still incredibly vibrant and interesting being made in 2026. So that's definitely saying something for the creativity and inventiveness of this product that it can be still so interesting after over 30 years. This is a lot of words for this, but it's also something that I care about quite a bit and quite like the highlights I would say here is the animation style. Everything about it just oozes quality the music's really cool. It's this funky jazz kind of thing, but it works. And the voice acting is really great. The number one most shocking thing of all is that the Major is being voiced by Maya Sakamoto holy crap she is incredible. She sounds so much like the original voice of the Major who did it for 20 years or whatever and I mean it's slightly different but it does not have the usual warmth of a Sakamoto role like she really, she really nailed it and in the best way of it sounding like the Major and not like her so props to sakamoto-san.

reviewed.titleEN: My Stepmother and Stepsisters Aren't Wicked
reviewed.titleJP: いびってこない義母と義姉
reviewed.ratingText: Never, Please No More Like This Ever
reviewed.review: So this show very much tells everything that you need to know about it in the title and then in the first couple minutes of the show, her mother dies. She's pretty much required to go and live with the stepmother and stuff. It's not good, but I actually kinda like some of the soundtrack in there. It was kind of cool like very bombastic classical music so that was cool. The rest was meh. Also, this is streaming on Prime exclusively in the US.

reviewed.titleJP: サンダー3
reviewed.review: So I'm kind of curious about this. The animation is very 3-D forward childish style, but they have these different character types within the same thing where the good-looking guys are way better than the main three characters are called the small three and they definitely fit that so I don't love the art style and such but I do find that there's something where I'm very curious about where it's gonna go at least in the first up and see from there

reviewed.titleJP: 二十世紀電氣目録-ユーレカ・エヴリカ-
reviewed.review: So cool show interesting setting late Meiji. And well done production from Kyoto Animation I'm curious to see where it goes. It could be good. I'm not sure if I'm gonna watch it just cause I feel like there are a lot and it's above trash watch level, but I'm not sure if it hits those sparks for me such as I'm definitely going to watch it, but it's nicely done and it looks to be a cool show with an interesting premise and a lot of cool artistic choices

fullReview.review: So I'm back and continue to watch more and I'm halfway through the first episode and it's very nicely produced and everything but for reason call it my fault I'm just not interested in it at all

reviewed.titleJP: 天は赤い河のほとり
reviewed.review:
I was actually kind of excited for this show since I've been reading some of the manga and think it's a cool art style and an interesting premise and that it takes a person back to effectively ancient Hittite empire, which is definitely an unexplored area in the isekai genre. 
Production seems pretty good on it. It's fine. I'm probably not gonna keep watching just cause it's OK but it's not really my thing but it's a cool kind of along the lines of 12 kingdoms.

reviewed.titleEN: Oh Boy, Was I Wrong About Her
reviewed.titleJP: 転校先の清楚可憐な美少女が、昔男子と思って一緒に遊んだ幼馴染だった件
reviewed.review: Oh boy well I think we've hit the bottom of the barrel of just terrible moments and whatever garbage it's really really just please please do not. More literal translation of the title is: "The Neat and Lovely Beautiful Girl at My Transfer School Turned Out to Be the Childhood Friend I Used to Play With, Who I Thought Was a Boy" (件/ken at the end is the light-novel-title convention marking it as "the matter/case of..."). So this shows that even at Crunchyroll they know this title and everything is so awful that even they had to summarize it as oh boy was I wrong about her, which is completely different from the title the perspective of the title and like everything so just so bad.

reviewed.titleEN: A Livid Lady's Guide to Getting Even: How I Crushed My Homeland with My Mighty Grimoires
reviewed.titleJP: ブチ切れ令嬢は報復を誓いました。 ～魔導書の力で祖国を叩き潰します～
reviewed.review:
The opening of this is literally copied from the opening of pardon me while I punch you show. So that show must've been very popular cause I think I've already seen two nearly identical clone shows that from this. So I'm sure it'll be something different rather than just punching and think this one based on the title will be magic or something as I watch the opening it looks pretty dumb, so we'll see where this goes in the next few minutes. 
So I've continue watching cause I was kind of curious to see where the hook was going and it's a fine trash show. Anticipate there will be some fun revenge. 
There's definitely something going on with these shows and the psyche that brings them about I think for some of these it feels like a rebellion against the status quo of the oligarchy and the insanely wealthy that are clearly and obviously corrupt and ruining these nice kingdoms/countries that we have for the people that actually live in them and work hard to keep them being nice places, but this could all be my interpretation of a silly show.

reviewed.titleEN: Heroine? Saint? No, I'm an All-Works Maid (And Proud of It)!
reviewed.titleJP: ヒロイン?聖女?いいえ、オールワークスメイドです(誇)!
reviewed.review: I don't understand why so many people are involved in producing this show. Apparently, the show has both a director and a supervising director really does not seem necessary. Seems like a couple of dedicated maid fetishes is all this show really needed and it certainly does not need me to watch it.

reviewed.titleJP: 岩元先輩ノ推薦
reviewed.ratingText: Never, Please No More Like This Ever
reviewed.review: the show is taking the familiar tropes of a Shinsengumi show and applying it to Taisho era imperial scenes. I feel like I've seen a few more things that are doing Taisho-era stuff lately which to me says that that's kind of a change in culture and where some various nostalgia and other cultural feelings rely so with that said the show itself is kind of boring me, and I'm not really interested in finding out more.

reviewed.titleJP: グロウアップショウ ～ひまわりのサーカス団～
reviewed.review: So we've now taken the world of cute girl band group thing, and moved it into the world of circuses in the showa time period. It looks like a fairly standard girl group thing show. No reason for me to watch more of this. I'm sure it's fine.

reviewed.titleJP: さよならララ
reviewed.review: OK so I did not have on my bingo board Kinema Citrus doing a 15th anniversary anime project as a version of the little mermaid and just totally killing it. This is a fabulous first episode. Everything was top-notch. I'm very curious where the rest of the show is going, but if just the first episode is great then that's worth the price of admission.

reviewed.titleEN: Young Ladies Don't Play Fighting Games
reviewed.titleJP: 対ありでした。～お嬢さまは格闘ゲームなんてしない～
reviewed.review: Well, I didn't mean to, but I did end up watching the entire first episode, so I guess that's something. I've been curious about it because it's a show about fighting games that was supposed to have a lot of actual game content, and they did a pretty good job delivering on that. The rest of the show is a nice-looking, well-done girls' high school dormitory show — it looks good, character designs are nice and clean, everything's well done. I feel like this could be my kind of trash show for the season, because it does a good job with fun fighting-game content and teaching the Japanese terms for a bunch of things, plus more details on fighting-game terminology and how to do things. It was fun.

fullReview.review: Finished two up to the show and it's pretty fun if I'm gonna watch a girls high school show I'd like to have it be dispersed with a bunch of fun streetfighter stuff. I also think it's pretty hilarious that everyone in the show goes so overboard comically injuring themselves doing ridiculous things like punching themselves in the face or jumping through windows so it's pretty fun show nicely produced characters are are fun. They definitely care about winning at streetfighter so it's a good summer show.

reviewed.titleJP: 天幕のジャードゥーガル
reviewed.review: This is definitely an interesting show. It's got such a unique, very non-standard anime art style, and the setting — early 1200s in Iran — is very cool and unique too, plus it deals with slavery and some of the economic and human issues, at least a little bit. It's very interesting. I didn't realize this was a Science SARU show, but I'm cool with it — they're doing a good job, so this one's got potential to actually be kind of cool.

reviewed.titleJP: 盗掘王
reviewed.review: So the character looks exactly like Solo Leveling, and I'm very confused about the language, because I just hit play as I always do and it appears to have the English track. So I'm curious if this is originally a Korean show… and I see that it is — there's Korean audio and English, no Japanese track, even though I feel like it's listed as Japanese. It's kind of weird, so I switched this to Korean and continued for a bit. Seems like a fine fantasy action show. I'm probably not going to continue, but there are worse things.

reviewed.titleJP: 鉄鍋のジャン！
reviewed.review:
I'm curious about this one based on the key art and the title, so let's see if it's fun or not.
So it's some sort of crazy cooking show based on a Chinese restaurant and Chinese cooking in Ginza. I'm not sure how I feel about it — honestly, I think it's probably fine and fun, but it's not something I'm super crazed about. So it's OK: if you're interested in that, it's reasonably well done and ridiculous.

reviewed.titleEN: From Overshadowed to Overpowered: Second Reincarnation of a Talentless Sage
reviewed.titleJP: 落第賢者の学院無双～二度目の転生、Sランクチート魔術師冒険録～
reviewed.review:
Here's hoping for some real trash anime based on the title, so we'll see if it disappoints or not.
Starting with a battle against the last boss: check.
Pan of a crowd: check.
Exposition as narration: check.
More crowd pans: check.
More bad pans in the opening: check.
Younger version of the main character looks very much like Kirito: check.
Slave-looking girl: check.

reviewed.titleJP: 令和のダラさん
reviewed.review: Seems like a perfectly fine, kind of dumb show. It's got a kind of funny premise — a horrible curse that's taken very seriously — and then the two teenagers don't care at all and just have fun with it, so it's fine. It's nothing I'll do more than watch in the background at this point, but I could be wrong. I'm just not going to be much help in finding out.

reviewed.titleJP: メビウス・ダスト
reviewed.ratingText: Never, Please No More Like This Ever
reviewed.review: It's kids with superpowers who can't use them, but then another kid has researched them and helps them figure out how to use them, blah blah blah blah blah. It's a show that has been produced and exists. It's not offensively bad, but it's also offensively not good.

reviewed.titleEN: Though I Am an Inept Villainess
reviewed.titleJP: ふつつかな悪女ではございますが ～雛宮蝶鼠とりかえ伝～
reviewed.review: So the show is kind of Freaky Friday set in an Apothecary Diaries-esque world. That's fine, I guess, but definitely not worth taking the time to watch.

reviewed.titleJP: レッツゴー怪奇組
reviewed.review: The show could actually be kind of fun. It's got sort of dorky-enough main characters, and the animation style is kind of interesting. It's a story about a guy who's super freaked out by ghosts — "at least six times the normal amount" — and then he meets a ghost and it doesn't scare him at all, and he's super disappointed. I'm hoping it could be a fun show. I don't think it's going to be anything spectacular, but you never know.

fullReview.review: So I watched three episodes of the four that have broadcast this thus far, and it's very fun. Good show. Definitely definitely a fun dorky show that takes itself appropriately and seriously. Nice production stuff throughout. I think it'll be a fun kind of low effort show for the season.

reviewed.titleEN: The Frontier Lord Begins with Zero Subjects
reviewed.titleJP: 領民0人スタートの辺境領主様
reviewed.review: Yeah, it's fine. It's at least not an isekai, which is great. The premise is actually kind of interesting: a guy gets sent out to this barren grassland as a reward for 20 years of combat, and it turns out there are people out there the whole time. Production seems pretty good, so it could actually be a decent show. Is it something I'm super interested in? I don't know, maybe? I haven't seen a single status screen or anything else that seems ridiculous, so it might be an actually legitimate fantasy show and not some other weird thing. The title is what put me off it, since it had so many words and all the dumb narou stuff in it, but it seems like it could actually be OK.

reviewed.titleEN: The Exiled Heavy Knight Knows How to Game the System
reviewed.titleJP: 追放された転生重騎士はゲーム知識で無双する
reviewed.review:
From the opening of this, I immediately identified it as a GoHands project, and I'm kind of bummed, because I generally liked their last show — I think they have some really cool visual style and things they do — so I'm bummed that it feels like such a bog-standard class-level-whatever, blah blah, show. I might still give this a watch just because I hope it at least looks cool and could be fun, but I don't know. I'm only two and a half minutes in, and we'll see where they get to in the next couple of minutes. …
So I ended up watching the full episode. The content itself feels like a fairly standard isekai thing. I guess I'll give them points for not actually bothering with the premise of having the person die or something — they just literally have the person say, "oh yeah, I remember playing this game and abusing it, and now I'm in the game, cool." I think the visuals worked well because GoHands is so over the top, and that's the only thing I think can make another bog-standard escapist-fantasy kind of show work, so I might actually keep watching it. It's not the greatest thing in the world, but it's at least fun, wild action.

fullReview.review: Watched two episodes of this and it's pretty fun trash. These shows are fun sometimes when they're done well and this one has enough of the crazy go hands, animation and as a fun premise so I'll watch it as a strictly trash, but delicious trash show.

reviewed.titleJP: バンドリ！ ゆめ∞みた
reviewed.ratingText: Never, Please No More Like This Ever
reviewed.review: I was not expecting to start with the words "new type." So I had this show on, half doing other stuff, but still paying attention. After eight minutes, I have no idea what this is. All I know is there were a lot of words, and I don't think they really meant anything. I'm definitely not interested in finding out — it's completely weird and bizarre, I don't even know. It feels like I'm in season eight of something, and it wouldn't matter even if I were.

reviewed.titleJP: 世界最強の後衛 ～迷宮国の新人探索者～
reviewed.review:
So this show is exactly what you'd think it's going to be — nothing is surprising, or gives any particular reason to watch it. You already have a lot of stills and non-moving background stuff within the first five minutes of the first episode, so that's a great sign.
I think the most interesting thing about this and all these similar shows is that it's another one where an office worker guy dies, and then all of a sudden he's reincarnated in another life as a JRPG person and joins a group of cute girls.
It's interesting to see that this is such a common fantasy that it's able to sell enough to keep getting so many shows produced in the same genre, with a nearly identical story, multiple times a quarter. I'm never quite sure exactly what it means, other than that there are enough Japanese salarymen who want to die and be reborn into a different life that giving them that isn't a bad business, I guess. I'm not sure there's anything particularly here or anything further to dig into, other than that the show shouldn't have been made — but it is interesting how many of these not-good shows are apparently cheap enough to make that they still turn a profit.
In summary, the episode is fine. It's awful. There's no way I'd keep watching the whole thing, but it's not offensively bad in any way other than being offensively "meh."

reviewed.titleEN: Smoking Behind the Supermarket with You
reviewed.titleJP: スーパーの裏でヤニ吸うふたり
reviewed.review: Smoking is back, baby! Between this and Yani Neko, it's all over the place. But this show was way better than that one. In fact, I watched the entire first episode, and it was fabulous — nicely done, good characters, interesting premise, no exposition, yet it still gave a clear sense of everything that was going on. Just a fabulous first episode. Seems like this show is kind of a halfway point between spring and summer, and the episodes are 15 minutes, so I'm quite looking forward to watching the rest of this.

reviewed.titleJP: 乙女怪獣キャラメリゼ
reviewed.review: The show's fine. It's a high school romance with a girl who's literally a monster, and turns into more of a kaiju when she gets emotional or whatever — similar to the movie Turning Red in that way. It's fine. I think it's totally watchable, at least at this point; seems like reasonable, decent production values, everything.

reviewed.titleJP: 猫と竜
reviewed.review:
Geez, this is definitely a mix of cute and heartbreaking, at least in the first part of the episode. I don't mind the exposition here, at least at this point, because it feels very much like a fairy-tale narration.
I'm still not quite sure exactly where the show is going or what it's going to do, but it's been done fairly well, and it's a little bit different in that it's got a bunch of talking magical creatures as the main characters, at least at this point — and, as is reasonable, humans are the enemy.

fullReview.review: So I watched two episodes of the show and it's super second screen material definitely nothing more than that. I don't know. I guess it's pleasant but there's nothing that makes me feel like I really care about anything that happens in any episode

reviewed.titleEN: Magical Girl Lyrical Nanoha EXCEEDS Gun Blaze Vengeance
reviewed.titleJP: 魔法少女リリカルなのは EXCEEDS Gun Blaze Vengeance
reviewed.review:
I think the crossed-front-hair thing looks more ridiculous on girls than it does on boys. I don't know why, maybe it's just this show. But the first episode is 15 minutes long, and I still don't know if that's longer than the actual title of the show.
I'm vaguely familiar with Magical Girl Lyrical Nanoha as a title from a mid-2000s or maybe 2010s show, but it wasn't one I ever watched, so I'm coming in here pretty clean. It's fine enough — is it something I'm going to go crazy for? Probably not, but it's better than a lot of the trash I've seen recently.
Ten minutes in, it's fine. It could be a fun action-adventure type show with demons and stuff, so seems reasonable.

reviewed.titleEN: Rich Girl Caretaker: I'm Secretly the Caregiver of the Most Popular Girl in This Rich Kid School
reviewed.titleJP: 才女のお世話 高嶺の花だらけな名門校で、学院一のお嬢様（生活能力皆無）を陰ながらお世話することになりました
reviewed.ratingText: Never, Please No More Like This Ever
reviewed.review: Maybe I'm getting jaded, but man, this sure is boring. Nothing, no reason for anything. The production is fine. Who cares.

reviewed.titleEN: The Duke's Son Claims He Won't Love Me Yet Showers Me with Adoration
reviewed.titleJP: 「きみを愛する気はない」と言った次期公爵様がなぜか溺愛してきます
reviewed.ratingText: Never, Please No More Like This Ever
reviewed.review:
Oh my God, it's another show with weird crossed-front-hair pretty-boy stuff. What is up with that hairstyle — it's like the unkempt look, but with the added weirdness of the very oddly long hair with crossed bangs in front of it? I think if you actually saw someone with that hair in person, it would look completely out of control, like you'd say that person is completely insane and unhinged. But I guess that's part of the fun of ridiculous anime character hair designs, all that stuff. It's a funny style that's super popular right now.
Why am I even talking about hair? Because the show itself is just so uninteresting — they literally had a line: "what a beautiful carrot."

reviewed.titleJP: 鬼の花嫁
reviewed.ratingText: Never, Please No More Like This Ever
reviewed.review: So the beginning of this is just a bunch of exposition about the world and all the things, blah blah blah blah blah. So if you're interested in a show where it literally says the greatest thing a woman can do is marry a demon, then this is the show for you — and for 2026.

reviewed.titleEN: Hanaori-san Still Wants to Fight in the Next Life
reviewed.titleJP: 花織さんは転生しても喧嘩がしたい
reviewed.review: This was fairly fun, actually — the first part of it is really just fast-paced dialogue between these two. It does have a weird reincarnation spin, but at least at this point it's kind of an entertaining take on it, where the demon lord was reincarnated and is just hanging out being a hikikomori, and then his nemesis shows up and she's crazy over the top. The production looks pretty decent — it's got a nicely stylized look and feel that seems pretty consistent throughout the opening and the rest of the production. So, is it going to be a great show? No, but it could actually be kind of fun, I'm sure. I'm curious if it's going to become a kind of adventure-of-the-week show, which could actually work fairly well for it, so I'll probably finish the episode and see if it's one I might potentially put on in the background — if I remember it, which means I probably won't watch it, but it's not the worst thing.

reviewed.titleEN: Love Unseen Beneath the Clear Night Sky
reviewed.titleJP: 透明な夜に駆ける君と、目に見えない恋をした。
reviewed.review: OK, so I started watching, and then I paused it and 10 minutes had passed. I'll definitely take that as a good sign. It's kind of interesting — it's about some folks who are new at college, meeting up at a mixer, I guess, and the hook is that one of the people at the party is blind. It goes from there. The production's decent enough — it actually seems to be done with a reasonable amount of care put into it in places, and the script seems pretty good, so I'm definitely going to finish the episode, since I'm already about halfway into it and curious to see where it goes. I think the characters seem realistic and interesting enough, so I definitely like the show more than I was expecting to, based on the length of the title.

fullReview.ratingText: I dictate all of my reviews
fullReview.review: Watched don’t show up so it’s a pretty charming show so the first little bit definitely continues to demonstrate what the overall show is so I like it. It’s a nice easy-going college romance that has some interesting stuff with the blind handicapped aspect to it definitely isn’t interesting it take that puts things out into an accessibility level and they cover things I think not being blind, but having dealt with a little bit and some pretty good presentation of the things so I like it. I think it’s a show that’s worth watching

reviewed.titleEN: The Insipid Prince's Furtive Grab for The Throne
reviewed.titleJP: 最強出涸らし皇子の暗躍帝位争い
reviewed.ratingText: Never, Please No More Like This Ever
reviewed.review:
So far the most notable thing about this is that the studio is Maho Film — which I take as a direct ahou reference, even though it's not, but it should be, because this is clearly made by a bunch of ahou. And I don't mean that as a compliment — I mean it: this is literally awful and completely ridiculous. Just some garbage, dime-a-dozen SS-class adventurer?!?! I mean, come on, this is ridiculous.

And these haircuts — they are really, really ridiculous. They're taking the unkempt-but-manicured look to a pretty ridiculous extreme. This show is just terrible. Don't watch it.

reviewed.titleEN: I Want to Love You Till Your Dying Day
reviewed.titleJP: きみが死ぬまで恋をしたい
reviewed.review: So I'm not quite sure where this is going — it might end up being a kind of high school assassin-romance thing — but particularly in comparison to the last few shows I watched, production values seem pretty decent. It started off without a giant pile of exposition; there was a little bit of monologue exposition, but it wasn't too crazy. Overall, I'm kind of curious to see where it goes, so I might finish this episode. I'm not anticipating it's going to be something super great, but it might be worth a second-screen watch, at least to finish the episode and see if it does anything cool that makes me want to keep watching.

fullReview.ratingText: I want to watch you on second screen
fullReview.review: I watched 3 1/2 episode of the show and it’s it’s quite fine but it’s also another orphan girl assassination show and this one has magic and all the things. The production value stay really high throughout. It’s a fine show, but it’s not one of those types of shows that capture me. Sometimes they do this one didn’t so for me, it’s more of a strictly second screen.

reviewed.titleEN: The Oblivious Saint Can't Contain Her Power
reviewed.titleJP: 無自覚聖女は今日も無意識に力を垂れ流す
reviewed.ratingText: Never, Please No More Like This Ever
reviewed.review:
OK, this is the first episode — you know, put your best foot forward — and the animation here is just so low-budget. Everything screams "paying the bills." Somehow it feels like a terrible version of "excuse me while I punch you in the face." The opening animation has tons of pans and stills and stupid small motions; it's all exposition and no good texturing. Oh boy. Oh boy.
It's not offensive, it's not anything — it should just not be.

reviewed.titleJP: 手札が多めのビクトリア
reviewed.review:
I'm so confused whether this is a continuing season or a new season.
It feels like each of the first ten or so scenes is a cut where you think, "okay, this is it, right before they play the opening" — and then they do a whole other one again.
I still don't really understand anything, in spite of this being basically constant exposition.
So I ended up getting through the five minutes — it's fine, I guess. I don't hate it; the animation and production values aren't great or anything, but that's OK. I just feel like I don't really know anything, and I'm not compelled to learn more. It's a very hard "meh."

reviewed.titleJP: これ描いて死ね
reviewed.review:
Very stylistically done — the production looks kind of cheap at first, but I don't think it is. I think it's literally just trying interesting stylistic choices.
Oh man, that manga shop looks super nice. I love it.
Definitely appreciate that they're putting a bit more effort into the subs on CR lately, so that's appreciated — the manga that's in there actually looks pretty good, like quite a bit like real manga.
Clearly they got licensing for a lot of this manga stuff, because they've got the real covers, really nicely rendered and everything in there, which is cool. So I'm five minutes in, and I'm not quite sure what the show is actually going to be, but it's got me curious about what it's going to be and where it's going.

fullReview.ratingText: here's hoping they have a horror manga episode
fullReview.review: Watch two episodes of the show and it's a pretty lovely put together homage to manga creation production stays nice and clean throughout. You get to see a girl becomes obsessed with Manga attempts to produce and make things it's it's very nicely done there's lots of co-production and sponsorship with tons of real mango so you see all the cool long spines pains buildings covers everything which is really nicely a nice touch to a thing that's about having it do that. Here's hoping to show stays interesting.

reviewed.titleJP: うちの弟どもがすみません
reviewed.review:
Oh boy, let's see how this goes…
What, no preparation or anything? Literally hiding that you're getting three brothers when you move into a house you didn't know anything about — but seems like they know all about her.
Wait, you literally haven't seen one of the brothers in a month even though he lives there? This is just terrible. She has younger brothers who are currently all a foot taller than her — very ridiculous.
Production is fine. You've got some kind of interesting palette and stuff going on. The direction is OK, but it's just not for me. How much more do I have? One minute left, I'll make it…

reviewed.titleEN: I Became a Legend After My 10 Year-Long Last Stand
reviewed.titleJP: ここは俺に任せて先に行けと言ってから10年がたったら伝説になっていた。
reviewed.review: It's actually potentially, maybe, not the worst thing in the first five minutes. I like it better than some of the other bog-standard garbage I've seen. I think the best thing about it is the soundtrack — it's got a real high-fantasy sound to it. Doesn't sound as good, but it's got that very Record of Lodoss War, old-fantasy-video-game feeling, which is good. Everything else about it, I'm not convinced it's going to go anywhere good, but I might keep it as a trash watch.

reviewed.titleJP: LV999の村人
reviewed.ratingText: Never, Please No More Like This Ever
reviewed.review:
Coming in here with the title and everything, I have zero hopes for the show, so let's see if there's anything worth watching. Oh good, a status screen to start off.
Shitty pan over nature, crappy water, a guy who's a teenager with black hair and an attitude.
Oh good, a level-three green slime and level-one villagers — note that there are title boxes over every single character and everything.
Note: all of these notes are from literally the first minute of the show.
Well, the animation for the opening was somehow even worse than the rest of it, and now we're getting into a description of classes.
I feel like at this point, shows like this are very self-selecting, kind of like a Nigerian prince scam, where the only people watching it are doing so knowing exactly what it is — it's not like you can watch this and not see that it's trash.
I was going to say something else here, but now my mind's a blank and I still have like a minute and a half left. I'm fairly certain I put more thought into this than was actually put into creating it, and now I have to suffer for the next minute and a half.

reviewed.titleJP: ワールド イズ ダンシング
reviewed.review:
So I'm a couple of minutes in, and I'm still not really sure what the show's about, but it's done with a good amount of care. What I mean is, I see a lot of background and minor characters, and they're actually drawn with moving parts, things moving fairly well, and good detail throughout.
So I'm definitely interested to see where this goes. It's set in old Japan, about a traveling dance troupe. I'm quite curious.

reviewed.titleJP: BLACK TORCH
reviewed.review:
Well, that took a radical change of tone from the first episode intro to about 10 seconds into the OP. It went from kind of an awkward kid-relationship thing, and now we're straight into hard-rock-and-action-looking shenanigans with swords and weapons and everything, and everyone is very hardcore.
I feel like they put all of their animation budget into the main character's neck — it's huge, makes Jotaro's neck look medium-sized. So it's now going to be some sort of, I don't know, fighting show or something, and he's going to be a cool ninja-fighter guy, and then he's going to learn and train and fight, and it's going to have animals and fight with them or against them, and it'll probably be fine, but meh.

reviewed.titleJP: 捨てられ聖女の異世界ごはん旅 隠れスキルでキャンピングカーを召喚しました
reviewed.ratingText: Never, Please No More Like This Ever
reviewed.review: If you've ever wondered what a bog-standard, stupid, no-reason-to-exist narou-kei isekai show is, this is the one for you. It's just complete trash. It's not good, it's not bad — everything is just ridiculous and stupid, and there's no point. I made that decision after the 30-second prologue, and then the opening definitely convinced me. It continues after that; apparently there's going to be 12 episodes of this, and there should've been zero. Oh, thank God, I survived the five minutes and it's over now.

reviewed.titleJP: ヤニねこ
reviewed.review: This is my first review of the summer season, and it's just as weird and depraved as I was thinking it was going to be — possibly even more so, I guess they advertised it correctly. Am I going to watch more of this? No. Is it awful? Yes. Could it potentially be a lowbrow, fun show? Yeah, it could be, but I'm not going to find out. So, season's off to a stunning start.

fullReview.ratingText: feels the same as smoking a pack of unfiltered camel 100s
fullReview.review: So I came back to this show was my first one of the season and I have ended up watching the first two episodes and probably gonna keep watching it now why why is that it? My thesis is that it’s not the show that we want but it is the show that we deserve for the year 2026. It is thoroughly depressing depraved. The characters have no redeeming value and yet we are entertained. So it’s definitely going to be my cigarette show of the season.
